A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Speedy-Splat. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original rendering, reconstruction-quality, compression, training-time, and pruning-score experiments in Section 5 and Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds pruning-percentage sweeps and a controlled comparison with StopThePop tile-based culling.

M1.justification: SnugBox, AccuTile, the efficient pruning score, and the pruning schedules and default percentages remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 removes a redundant initialization of the tile counter without changing its behavior.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine Mip-NeRF 360 scenes, two Tanks & Temples scenes, and two Deep Blending scenes. The added experiments vary pruning and rendering configurations within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds a targeted comparison against StopThePop's Tile-Based Culling component with warp-level load balancing in Tables 7–8. The comparator sets in the retained pruning comparisons are unchanged; the new experiment does not evaluate the full StopThePop renderer.

E3.justification: Appendix A.2 introduces a two-dimensional sweep of hard pruning from 0–40% and soft pruning at 0% and 50–95%, in 5% increments, with localization disabled. Appendix A.4 introduces matched-model timing across three renderers, including a culling configuration without a padded alpha threshold. Existing experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V1 primarily shows cumulative component additions and a pruning-score comparison. V2 adds isolated and joint pruning sensitivity analyses in Figure 7, plus function-level and per-scene culling ablations in Tables 7–8. These directly examine pruning interactions and the source of localization speed advantages.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over three independent runs and repeated test-set rendering for timing. The added experiments continue these averaging practices; v2 introduces no confidence intervals, dispersion reporting, significance tests, or increased run counts for retained experiments.

E6.justification: V2 adds six-metric pruning response surfaces and new culling timings: Table 7 reports 3.660 ms for AccuTile versus 4.051 ms for Tile-Based Culling, with AccuTile faster on every scene in Table 8. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1 scores. Tables 1–6 and all retained per-scene numerical results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds a case-based AccuTile correctness sketch covering different ellipse–row boundary configurations and symmetry for columns. It develops the monotonicity reasoning already present in v1 Section 4.1.2; the mathematical definitions, equations, and pruning derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract now emphasizes rendering speed and calls compression and training benefits ancillary. However, the introduction and conclusion retain the same four contributions and headline speed, compression, and training claims, including 6.71× rendering acceleration and 10.6× fewer primitives.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the 80%/30% pruning choice as a speed–quality compromise. Appendix A.4 explains the culling runtime gap through candidate-tile iteration and attributes StopThePop's small downstream timing advantages to undercounted mappings. Section 6's existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-page link, explicitly identifies Table 3's comparator scores as published results, and documents integrating StopThePop culling code with warp-level load balancing and no padded alpha threshold. These are additional access, provenance, and implementation disclosures.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds StopThePop, 3DGS-MCMC, and several densification and structured-Gaussian works. It revises the FlashGS discussion from lower overall speed attributed to absent pruning to its similarity with StopThePop, while positioning AccuTile through the new culling comparison. The broader research framing remains intact.

P1.justification: V2 edits the abstract, introduction, and several pruning explanations, corrects wording and redundant pseudocode, and expands the appendix organization. The main section sequence and most methodological and results prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds ellipse-case illustrations, a six-panel pruning heatmap, and two culling timing tables. Figure 6 reuses the Figure 2 example. Retained dataset tables are arranged side by side, and the unchanged per-scene tables are relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the central contributions: the pruning sweep tests component interactions and parameter choices, while the matched-model culling comparison addresses a missing close comparator. The correctness sketch and clearer implementation disclosures further improve assessability. The missing padded threshold limits conclusions about equivalent rendering accuracy, but this disclosed caveat does not outweigh the substantial validation gains; the original evidence is retained.
